To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the X-ray light curve of 3C390.3 exhibits a non-stationary behavior, with the variability properties varying in a correlated fashion with changes in the energy spectrum; (2) this behavior is similar to that observed in Galactic black hole binaries in the hard state; (3) this is the first time this behavior has been detected in AGN.

the X-ray light curve of 3C390.3 is consistent with being non-stationary, and the characteristic time scale of variability decreases as energy spectrum softens, in the same manner as Galactic black hole binaries.

the X-ray variability of 3C390.3 changes with energy in a way that is similar to the behavior of Galactic black hole binaries, and that the characteristic time-scale for X-ray variability decreases with energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the temporal properties of X-ray light curves of AGN.
the study of the variability properties of the X-ray light curves of AGN.
the study of the temporal properties of the X-ray variability in the radio galaxy 3C 273, using data obtained with the Rossi X-Ray Timing Explorer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the variability properties (in terms of the characteristic time-scale, and possibly also the power spectral density shape) of the source are not constant, and that this is a common feature of AGNs.
3C 39.3 shows evidence for correlated spectral and temporal changes, and this is the first time such behavior is detected in the X-ray band.
we have found evidence for a new link between the temporal and spectral changes of AGN and Galactic binaries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the variability properties in 3C390.3 are similar to those of black hole binaries in the low/hard state.
the variability properties in the hard state of Galactic black hole binaries and in 3C390.3 are similar.
the X-ray variability characteristics of 3C390.3 are consistent with the picture that the accretion flow in this AGN is similar to that in the hard state of the Galactic black hole binaries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
non-linear analysis methods are very useful in detecting non-stationarity.

, if the analogy between Galactic black hole binaries and AGN is correct, we should expect to find evidence of non-steady state behavior in the temporal properties (i.e., time scales and amplitudes) of AGN light curves.

the scaling index technique, which is based on the non-linear properties of the data, can provide a more sensitive probe of non-stationary time series than the linear techniques that are currently in use.
